question: The 91st Amendment Act, 2003 of the Indian Constitution is related with which of the following?
option_1: Limiting the size of the Council of Ministers
option_2: No enhancement of seats of Lok sabha and vidhan sabha til 2026
option_3: Bifurcation of the National commission of SC and ST
option_4: Fixed the strength of the Goa Legislative Assembly at a minimum of 30 members
solution_text:
The correct answer is Limiting the size of the Council of Ministers.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The 91st Constitutional Amendment Act, 2003 (91वाँ संविधान संशोधन अधिनियम) limited the size of the Council of Ministers (मंत्रिपरिषद).

• It provides that the total number of Ministers, including the Prime Minister, in the Central Council of Ministers shall not exceed 15% of the total strength of the Lok Sabha.

• At the State level, the total number of Ministers, including the Chief Minister, shall not exceed 15% of the total strength of the Legislative Assembly, subject to a minimum of 12 Ministers.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The Amendment also inserted an anti-defection safeguard: a defector is disqualified from holding a ministerial or remunerative political post.

• It strengthened the Tenth Schedule (Anti-Defection Law) by removing the earlier provision that exempted 'splits' in a party.

• It added Articles 75(1A), 164(1A) and 361B to the Constitution.

NOTE

• No enhancement of seats of Lok sabha and vidhan sabha til 2026 (Option 2): This freezing of seats relates to the 84th Amendment Act, 2001 (later extended), not the 91st.

• Bifurcation of the National commission of SC and ST (Option 3): The splitting of the combined commission into separate NCSC and NCST was done by the 89th Amendment Act, 2003.

• Fixed the strength of the Goa Legislative Assembly at a minimum of 30 members (Option 4): This provision came through earlier amendments concerning Goa's statehood (Goa, Daman and Diu Reorganisation Act, 1987 era), not the 91st Amendment.

question: The 'Kaladan Multi Modal Transit Transport' Project is associated with which of the following country?
solution_text:
The correct answer is India and Myanmar.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Kaladan Multi-Modal Transit Transport Project (कलादान मल्टी मॉडल ट्रांजिट ट्रांसपोर्ट परियोजना) is a joint project between India and Myanmar.

• It aims to connect the eastern Indian seaport of Kolkata with Sittwe port in Myanmar, and further link Mizoram through river and road transport.

• It provides an alternative route to India's North-Eastern states, reducing dependence on the narrow Siliguri (Chicken's Neck) Corridor.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• The project uses sea route (Kolkata to Sittwe), river route (Sittwe to Paletwa on the Kaladan river) and road route (Paletwa to Zorinpui in Mizoram).

• It was framework-agreed in 2008 and is aligned with India's 'Act East Policy'.

• Sittwe Port lies in the Rakhine State of Myanmar.

NOTE

• India and Nepal (Option 1): Cooperation with Nepal involves projects like the Integrated Check Posts and cross-border rail links (e.g., Jaynagar–Kurtha), not Kaladan.

• India and Pakistan (Option 2): No such transit corridor project exists between the two; connectivity is minimal (e.g., Attari-Wagah).

• India and Bangladesh (Option 3): India–Bangladesh connectivity is served by projects like the Akhaura–Agartala rail link and inland waterways protocol, not Kaladan.

question: As of March 2024, the G-20 members represent around _____ of the global GDP.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 85%.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• As of March 2024, the members of the G-20 (जी-20) collectively represent around 85% of the global GDP (वैश्विक जीडीपी).

• The G-20 also accounts for about 75% of global trade and roughly two-thirds (about 67%) of the world's population.

• It is the premier forum for international economic cooperation among major developed and developing economies.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• The G-20 was founded in 1999 (as a finance ministers' forum) and the first leaders' summit was held in 2008.

• India held the G-20 Presidency in 2023, with the summit held in New Delhi under the theme 'Vasudhaiva Kutumbakam' (One Earth, One Family, One Future).

• The African Union was admitted as a permanent member of the G-20 during India's presidency in 2023.

NOTE

• 25% (Option 1): Far too low; this underestimates the G-20's economic weight.

• 40% (Option 2): Incorrect; the G-20's share of global GDP is much higher.

• 62% (Option 3): Incorrect; this figure understates the actual share of around 85%.

question: Who was elected as the first woman president of the Indian Olympic Association (IOA) in 2022?
solution_text:
The correct answer is PT Usha.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• P.T. Usha (पी.टी. उषा) was elected as the first woman President of the Indian Olympic Association (IOA) in 2022.

• Known as the 'Payyoli Express' and 'Queen of Indian Track and Field', she is a legendary sprinter from Kerala.

• She is also a nominated Member of the Rajya Sabha.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• At the 1984 Los Angeles Olympics, she narrowly missed a bronze medal in the 400m hurdles, finishing fourth by 1/100th of a second.

• She won multiple gold medals at the Asian Games and Asian Championships during the 1980s.

• She was awarded the Arjuna Award and the Padma Shri.

NOTE

• Annu Rani (Option 1): She is an Indian javelin thrower, the national record holder, not an IOA president.

• Ashapurna Devi (Option 3): She was a Bengali novelist and the first woman to win the Jnanpith Award (1976); unrelated to the IOA.

• Hima Das (Option 4): She is a sprinter ('Dhing Express') and the first Indian woman to win gold at a World U-20 Athletics Championships; not an IOA president.

question: Who became the Chief Election Commissioner of India in February 2025?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Gyanesh Kumar.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Gyanesh Kumar (ज्ञानेश कुमार) became the Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) of India in February 2025.

• He succeeded Rajiv Kumar, who demitted office in February 2025.

• He was the first CEC appointed under the new Chief Election Commissioner and Other Election Commissioners (Appointment, Conditions of Service and Term of Office) Act, 2023.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The CEC and Election Commissioners are appointed by the President of India.

• As per Article 324, the Election Commission of India is a constitutional body responsible for conducting elections.

• The CEC can be removed only through the same process as a Supreme Court judge (by impeachment).

NOTE

• Rajiv Kumar (Option 1): He was the CEC who preceded Gyanesh Kumar and retired in February 2025.

• Sukhbir Singh Sandhu (Option 2): He was serving as an Election Commissioner, not the CEC appointed in February 2025.

• Anup Chandra Pandey (Option 4): He was a former Election Commissioner who had retired earlier (February 2024).

question: Which year marks two decades since the launch of the ASHA programme?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 2025.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The ASHA (Accredited Social Health Activist) programme (आशा कार्यक्रम) was launched in 2005 under the National Rural Health Mission (NRHM).

• Two decades (20 years) since its launch in 2005 falls in the year 2025.

• ASHA workers are community health volunteers who act as a link between the community and the public health system.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• ASHAs are primarily women residents of the village they serve, selected and accountable to the local community.

• In 2022, India's ASHA workers were honoured with the WHO Director-General's Global Health Leaders Award.

• The programme is a key component of the National Health Mission (NHM).

NOTE

• 2019 (Option 1): This would mark only about 14 years since the 2005 launch, not two decades.

• 2022 (Option 2): This marks about 17 years; also the year ASHAs received the WHO award, but not two decades.

• 2023 (Option 3): This marks about 18 years since launch, not two decades.

question: What is the primary objective of the Subhadra Yojana launched by Odisha Government?
option_1: To provide housing amenities to women
option_2: To give financial assistance of Rs. 50000 over five years to women aged 21-60
option_3: To offer educational scholarships to female students
option_4: To support women entrepreneurs with loans
solution_text:
The correct answer is To give financial assistance of Rs. 50000 over five years to women aged 21-60.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Subhadra Yojana (सुभद्रा योजना) was launched by the Government of Odisha to provide financial assistance of Rs. 50,000 over five years to eligible women aged 21 to 60 years.

• Under the scheme, Rs. 10,000 per year is given in two instalments of Rs. 5,000 each.

• It is a women's empowerment (महिला सशक्तिकरण) direct-benefit scheme.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The scheme was launched in September 2024 by the Odisha Government.

• The money is transferred directly to the Aadhaar-enabled bank accounts of beneficiaries (Direct Benefit Transfer).

• Beneficiaries receive a Subhadra debit card.

NOTE

• To provide housing amenities to women (Option 1): Housing benefits are provided under schemes like PMAY, not the primary aim of Subhadra Yojana.

• To offer educational scholarships to female students (Option 3): Scholarships fall under education schemes, not this cash-transfer scheme.

• To support women entrepreneurs with loans (Option 4): Credit/loan support is offered under schemes like Mudra Yojana; Subhadra gives direct cash assistance, not loans.

question: Prakash Padukone is related to which of the following sports?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Badminton.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Prakash Padukone (प्रकाश पादुकोण) is a legendary Indian badminton (बैडमिंटन) player.

• In 1980, he became the first Indian to win the prestigious All England Open Badminton Championships.

• He also reached World No. 1 ranking in badminton.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• He was awarded the Arjuna Award (1972) and the Padma Shri (1982).

• He runs the Prakash Padukone Badminton Academy in Bengaluru, which has produced many top players.

• He is the father of Bollywood actress Deepika Padukone.

NOTE

• Football (Option 1): Indian football icons include Sunil Chhetri and Bhaichung Bhutia, not Prakash Padukone.

• Hockey (Option 2): Hockey legends include Dhyan Chand and Balbir Singh Sr.

• Shooting (Option 3): Prominent Indian shooters include Abhinav Bindra and Gagan Narang.

question: The Board of Control for Cricket in India was established in the year _____.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1928.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Board of Control for Cricket in India (BCCI / भारतीय क्रिकेट कंट्रोल बोर्ड) was established in 1928.

• It is the national governing body for cricket in India and is headquartered in Mumbai.

• It is registered as a society under the Tamil Nadu Societies Registration Act.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The BCCI is affiliated to the International Cricket Council (ICC).

• Its first president was R. E. Grant Govan.

• The BCCI organises the Indian Premier League (IPL), Ranji Trophy, and other domestic tournaments.

NOTE

• 1908 (Option 2): Incorrect; the BCCI did not exist then.

• 1958 (Option 3): Incorrect; this is decades after the actual founding year.

• 1968 (Option 4): Incorrect; the BCCI was already well established by this time.

question: 20th National Youth Athletics Championships 2025 was held in which city?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Patna.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The 20th National Youth Athletics Championships 2025 (20वीं राष्ट्रीय युवा एथलेटिक्स चैंपियनशिप) was held in Patna, Bihar.

• It was organised under the aegis of the Athletics Federation of India (AFI).

• Patna is the capital city of Bihar, situated on the banks of the river Ganga.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The championship features young athletes in the under-16/youth age category.

• The Athletics Federation of India (AFI) is the apex body governing athletics in the country.

• Bihar has been increasingly hosting national-level sporting events in recent years.

NOTE

• Mumbai (Option 2): The capital of Maharashtra; it did not host this edition of the championship.

• Ranchi (Option 3): The capital of Jharkhand; not the venue for this event.

• Surat (Option 4): A major city in Gujarat known for textiles and diamonds; not the host city.

question: Which of the following musical instrument is a 'wind instrument' made of wood and metal?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Mahuri.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Mahuri (माहुरी) is a traditional wind instrument (सुषिर वाद्य) made of wood and metal, popular in Odisha.

• It resembles the shehnai and is a double-reed aerophone.

• It is commonly played during festivals, marriages and folk performances.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Wind instruments (aerophones/sushir vadya) produce sound by vibration of air, e.g., flute, shehnai, mahuri.

• The Mahuri is an important accompaniment in Odissi and folk music of eastern India.

• Its body is typically wooden with a metallic flared bell at the end.

NOTE

• Dhak (Option 1): A large membranophone (percussion drum) played especially during Durga Puja, not a wind instrument.

• Sarang / Sarangi (Option 3): A bowed string instrument (chordophone), not a wind instrument.

• Mridangam (Option 4): A double-headed percussion drum used in Carnatic music, not a wind instrument.

question: Who won the Pulitzer Prize for the debut work 'Interpreter of Maladies', published in 1999?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Jhumpa Lahiri.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Jhumpa Lahiri (झुम्पा लाहिड़ी) won the Pulitzer Prize for Fiction (पुलित्जर पुरस्कार) in 2000 for her debut short-story collection 'Interpreter of Maladies' (published 1999).

• It was her first book and an unusual instance of a debut collection winning the Pulitzer.

• She is an Indian-American author known for themes of the immigrant experience.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Her novel 'The Namesake' (2003) was adapted into a film by Mira Nair.

• Her later works include 'Unaccustomed Earth' and 'The Lowland' (shortlisted for the Man Booker Prize).

• She was awarded the National Humanities Medal by the United States.

NOTE

• Kiran Desai (Option 1): She won the Man Booker Prize in 2006 for 'The Inheritance of Loss', not the Pulitzer for Interpreter of Maladies.

• Shobha Rao (Option 3): An Indian-American author of works like 'An Unrestored Woman'; not the winner of this prize.

• Chitra Banerjee Divakaruni (Option 4): An author of novels like 'The Mistress of Spices'; not the author of Interpreter of Maladies.

question:
The Patiala Gharana is notable for its rendering of which types of classical music?
I. Thumri
II. Khyal
solution_text:
The correct answer is Both I and II.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Patiala Gharana (पटियाला घराना) is notable for its rendering of both Thumri (ठुमरी) and Khyal (ख्याल) forms of Hindustani classical music.

• It is known for intricate ornamentation, fast taans, and emotive delivery.

• Hence both statements I and II are correct.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The Patiala Gharana was founded by Ustad Fateh Ali Khan and Ustad Ali Baksh Khan (known as 'Aliya-Fattu').

• Ustad Bade Ghulam Ali Khan is its most celebrated exponent.

• Khyal and Thumri are important vocal genres of Hindustani classical music.

NOTE

• Only I (Option 1): Incorrect, because the gharana is renowned for Khyal as well, not just Thumri.

• Only II (Option 2): Incorrect, because it is famous for Thumri as well as Khyal.

• Neither I nor II (Option 4): Incorrect, because both Thumri and Khyal are hallmarks of the Patiala Gharana.

question: Who is the author of the book 'Marx's Revenge: The Resurgence of Capitalism and the Death of Statist Socialism'?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Meghnad Desai.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Meghnad Desai (मेघनाद देसाई) is the author of 'Marx's Revenge: The Resurgence of Capitalism and the Death of Statist Socialism'.

• He is a noted economist (अर्थशास्त्री) and a former British House of Lords member of Indian origin.

• The book analyses the evolution of capitalism and the decline of state-controlled socialism.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Lord Meghnad Desai was associated with the London School of Economics (LSE).

• He was awarded the Padma Bhushan by the Government of India in 2008.

• His other works include 'The Rediscovery of India' and a biography of Dilip Kumar.

NOTE

• Amartya Sen (Option 1): Nobel laureate economist and author of works like 'The Argumentative Indian' and 'Development as Freedom'; not this book.

• Pavan K. Varma (Option 3): A diplomat and author of books like 'The Great Indian Middle Class'; not the author of this work.

• Ramachandra Guha (Option 4): A historian and author of 'India After Gandhi'; not the author of Marx's Revenge.

question: 'Gaan-Ngai' festival is celebrated in which of the following state?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Manipur.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The 'Gaan-Ngai' festival (गान-नगाई त्योहार) is celebrated in the state of Manipur (मणिपुर).

• It is a major post-harvest festival of the Zeliangrong community (Rongmei Naga people).

• It marks the beginning of the new year and involves feasting, folk dances and songs.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Manipur is a north-eastern state whose capital is Imphal.

• Other festivals of Manipur include Yaoshang, Lai Haraoba, and Ningol Chakouba.

• The Sangai deer and the Loktak Lake are famous natural landmarks of Manipur.

NOTE

• Kerala (Option 1): Its notable festivals include Onam and Vishu, not Gaan-Ngai.

• Maharashtra (Option 3): Its major festivals include Ganesh Chaturthi and Gudi Padwa.

• Andhra Pradesh (Option 4): Its festivals include Ugadi and Sankranti, not Gaan-Ngai.

question: In the context of Hindu temple architecture, the place where the main idol of a deity is placed is known as _____.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Garbhagriha.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In Hindu temple architecture, the Garbhagriha (गर्भगृह) or 'sanctum sanctorum' is the innermost chamber where the main idol of the deity is placed.

• It is a small, usually windowless and dark chamber, symbolising a womb ('garbha' = womb, 'griha' = house).

• Only the priest is generally allowed to enter this most sacred space.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The Garbhagriha is typically located directly beneath the temple's tallest tower.

• The concept developed in the Gupta period and matured in later Nagara and Dravida styles.

• The path for circumambulation around it is called the Pradakshina Patha.

NOTE

• Mandapa (Option 2): A pillared hall or porch in front of the sanctum where devotees gather, not where the idol is placed.

• Shikhara (Option 3): The rising tower/spire (in Nagara style) above the sanctum, not the idol chamber itself.

• Vaahan (Option 4): The mount or vehicle of a deity (e.g., Nandi for Shiva), not a part of temple structure housing the idol.

question: 'Veeragase' is a traditional folk dance of which Indian state?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Karnataka.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Veeragase (वीरगासे) is a vigorous traditional folk dance of the state of Karnataka (कर्नाटक).

• It is a dance based on Hindu mythology, associated with the worship of Lord Shiva and Goddess Shakti.

• It is performed during the months of Shravana and Kartika, and is part of the Dasara procession in Mysuru.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The dancers, called Veeragase or Lingadevaru, wear vibrant costumes and carry symbols of Lord Shiva.

• Other folk dances of Karnataka include Yakshagana, Dollu Kunitha and Kamsale.

• The dance is known for its energetic and intense (veera = valour) movements.

NOTE

• Bihar (Option 2): Its folk dances include Jat-Jatin and Jhijhian, not Veeragase.

• Tripura (Option 3): Its folk dances include Hojagiri, not Veeragase.

• Jharkhand (Option 4): Its folk dances include Paika and Chhau, not Veeragase.

question: As part of Mission Mausam, India is building a cloud chamber at which institute?
option_4: Indian Institute of Tropical Meteorology, Pune
solution_text:
The correct answer is Indian Institute of Tropical Meteorology, Pune.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• As part of Mission Mausam (मिशन मौसम), India is building a cloud chamber (क्लाउड चैंबर) at the Indian Institute of Tropical Meteorology (IITM), Pune.

• The cloud chamber will help scientists study cloud physics and advance cloud-seeding and weather-modification research.

• Mission Mausam aims to make India 'weather-ready and climate-smart'.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Mission Mausam was approved by the Union Cabinet in September 2024 under the Ministry of Earth Sciences.

• It focuses on improving weather forecasting, observation networks, radars and satellites.

• IITM Pune is a premier institute under the Ministry of Earth Sciences.

NOTE

• Indian Institute of Science (IISc), Bengaluru (Option 1): A leading research institute, but not the site of the Mission Mausam cloud chamber.

• Indian Institute of Technology, Delhi (Option 2): A premier engineering institute; not associated with this cloud chamber.

• National Physical Laboratory, New Delhi (Option 3): India's measurement standards laboratory; not the cloud chamber site.

question: There are how many sectors are covered in Production linked Incentive (PLI) Scheme launched in August 2023?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 14.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Production Linked Incentive (PLI) Scheme (उत्पादन आधारित प्रोत्साहन योजना) covers 14 sectors.

• The scheme provides financial incentives on incremental sales of goods manufactured in India to boost domestic manufacturing.

• It is a key pillar of the 'Atmanirbhar Bharat' (self-reliant India) initiative.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The 14 sectors include mobiles/electronics, pharmaceuticals, telecom, textiles, automobiles and auto components, ACC batteries, food products, white goods, and others.

• The scheme is implemented by respective ministries with an overall large outlay.

• It aims to make Indian manufacturers globally competitive and reduce import dependence.

NOTE

• 11 (Option 1): Incorrect; the PLI scheme covers 14 sectors, not 11.

• 21 (Option 3): Incorrect; this overstates the number of PLI sectors.

• 25 (Option 4): Incorrect; the correct number of sectors is 14.

question: The foreign exchange reserve of India dropped to levels that were _____ during 1991 economic crisis
option_1: not sufficient for even a fortnight
solution_text:
The correct answer is not sufficient for even a fortnight.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• During the 1991 economic crisis (1991 का आर्थिक संकट), India's foreign exchange reserves fell so low that they were not sufficient for even a fortnight (पंद्रह दिन) of essential imports.

• A fortnight means a period of about two weeks (15 days).

• This balance-of-payments crisis forced India to pledge its gold reserves and seek IMF assistance.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The crisis led to the launch of the 1991 economic reforms (LPG reforms — Liberalisation, Privatisation, Globalisation).

• P. V. Narasimha Rao was the Prime Minister and Dr. Manmohan Singh was the Finance Minister at that time.

• India airlifted gold to the Bank of England to raise emergency foreign exchange.

NOTE

• not sufficient for twenty days (Option 2): Incorrect; reserves were critically lower, barely enough for two weeks.

• not sufficient for thirty days (Option 3): Incorrect; the actual crunch was far more severe (under a fortnight).

• not sufficient for fifty days (Option 4): Incorrect; this overstates the reserves available during the crisis.

question: For how many years does the President of India hold office?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 5 years.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The President of India (भारत का राष्ट्रपति) holds office for a term of five (5) years from the date on which he/she enters office.

• This is provided under Article 56 of the Indian Constitution.

• The President is eligible for re-election and there is no limit on the number of terms.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The President is elected by an Electoral College consisting of elected members of both Houses of Parliament and elected members of State/UT Legislative Assemblies (Article 54).

• The President can resign by addressing the resignation letter to the Vice-President.

• The President can be removed through impeachment for 'violation of the Constitution' under Article 61.

NOTE

• 3 years (Option 1): Incorrect; the constitutional term is five years, not three.

• 4 years (Option 2): Incorrect; four years is not the term for the Indian President.

• 6 years (Option 4): Incorrect; six years is the term associated with Rajya Sabha members, not the President.

question: The Parliament of India can legislate on a state subject if _____.
option_2: Council of state passes a resolution by 2/3 majority of the members present
option_3: Lok Sabha passes a resolution by simple majority
option_4: Rajya Sabha passes a resolution by simple majority
solution_text:
The correct answer is Council of state passes a resolution by 2/3 majority of the members present.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Under Article 249, the Parliament (संसद) can legislate on a State subject if the Rajya Sabha (Council of States / राज्य परिषद) passes a resolution supported by a two-thirds (2/3) majority of the members present and voting, declaring it necessary in the national interest.

• Such a law remains in force for a period of one year and can be extended.

• This is one of the special powers of the Rajya Sabha.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Other situations where Parliament can legislate on State subjects: during a National Emergency (Article 250), with consent of two or more States (Article 252), and to implement international treaties/agreements (Article 253).

• Subjects are divided into the Union List, State List and Concurrent List under the Seventh Schedule.

• Article 249 resolutions add flexibility to the federal distribution of powers.

NOTE

• The President issues an ordinance (Option 1): An ordinance (Article 123) is temporary legislation and cannot override the normal division of legislative powers on state subjects.

• Lok Sabha passes a resolution by simple majority (Option 3): This power lies with the Rajya Sabha (by 2/3 majority), not the Lok Sabha by simple majority.

• Rajya Sabha passes a resolution by simple majority (Option 4): Incorrect, because Article 249 requires a two-thirds majority, not a simple majority.

question: Among the following organs, which is located on uppermost part of a human body?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Buccal Cavity.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Among the given organs, the Buccal Cavity (मुख गुहिका), i.e., the mouth cavity, is located on the uppermost part of the human body.

• It is the beginning of the alimentary canal (digestive tract), where digestion starts.

• It contains the teeth, tongue and salivary glands.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Digestion of starch begins in the buccal cavity through the enzyme salivary amylase (ptyalin).

• The alimentary canal runs from mouth → oesophagus → stomach → small intestine → large intestine → anus.

• The buccal cavity is located in the head, the topmost region among these organs.

NOTE

• Anus (Option 2): The lowermost opening of the alimentary canal, through which faeces are eliminated.

• Bile Duct (Option 3): A tube carrying bile from the liver/gall bladder to the small intestine, located in the mid-abdomen.

• Appendix (Option 4): A small vestigial tube attached to the large intestine (caecum) in the lower abdomen.

question:
Which of the following organ is part of excretory system in human body?
I. A pair of ureters
II. A urethra
solution_text:
The correct answer is Both I and II.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In the human excretory system (उत्सर्जन तंत्र), both a pair of ureters (मूत्रवाहिनी) and the urethra (मूत्रमार्ग) are essential organs.

• The ureters carry urine from the two kidneys to the urinary bladder.

• The urethra carries urine from the urinary bladder out of the body.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The main organs of the human excretory system are: two kidneys, two ureters, one urinary bladder, and one urethra.

• The kidneys filter blood and form urine through structures called nephrons (the functional units).

• Excretion removes nitrogenous wastes like urea from the body.

NOTE

• Only I (Option 1): Incorrect, because the urethra is also part of the excretory system, not just the ureters.

• Only II (Option 2): Incorrect, because the ureters are equally part of the excretory system.

• Neither I nor II (Option 4): Incorrect, because both the ureters and the urethra belong to the excretory system.

question: Around the _____th century BCE, Mahāpadma Nanda rose to prominence in Magadha.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 5.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Mahāpadma Nanda (महापद्मनंद) was the founder of the powerful Nanda dynasty (नंद वंश) of Magadha (मगध).

• As per the option marked in the official key, he is placed as rising to prominence around the 5th century BCE.

• He overthrew the Shishunaga dynasty and greatly expanded the Magadhan empire.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Mahapadma Nanda is described in the Puranas as 'Sarva-Kshatrantaka' (destroyer of all Kshatriyas) and 'Ekarat' (sole sovereign).

• The last Nanda ruler, Dhana Nanda, was overthrown by Chandragupta Maurya with the help of Chanakya (Kautilya).

• The Nanda dynasty was known for its large army and immense wealth.

NOTE

• 1 (Option 1): The 1st century BCE is far too late; the Nandas had long been replaced by the Mauryas by then.

• 2 (Option 2): The 2nd century BCE corresponds to the post-Mauryan (Shunga) period, not the rise of the Nandas.

• 3 (Option 3): The 3rd century BCE is the era of the Maurya empire (Ashoka), after the Nandas had already fallen.
